title: Internship Applications Open
summary_text: The Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Undergraduate Internship Program applications open today. Learn more at sustainability.tamu.edu.
description_text:
The goal of the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Internship Program is to bring undergraduate students from a variety of backgrounds and perspectives together to create a dynamic team that works to create a culture of sustainability at Texas A&M University. Interns work together to increase awareness and education about the three pillars of sustainability: environmental, economic, and social. The team focuses on educating the campus community about topics such as: energy and water use, transportation, food services, construction and built environment, purchasing, recycling, and social sustainability through the development of outreach initiatives and event coordination. Additionally, interns support assessment and planning efforts prioritized by the office.

The Internship Program is open to any TAMU undergraduate student and all majors are encouraged to apply because true sustainability must be an interdisciplinary enterprise.

Applications are open October 6, 2025 – November 9, 2025 at sustainability.tamu.edu.

title: Stream Clean
location: Parking Lot 97 off John Kimbrough Blvd
summary_text: Environmental Health & Safety provide Stream Clean as a service opportunity for campus members to volunteer their time cleaning litter and debris from campus streams. All students, faculty and staff are welcome to participate, and any student organization can register their group.
description_text:
All Aggies who participate will earn FIVE entries into our CSM Grand Prize Giveaway with winners announced November 7.

Volunteers should wear long pants and closed-toed shoes, as you may be walking through tall grass and weeds. Each volunteer will be supplied with a pair of gloves, a litter picker, and a garbage bag to assist with picking up trash and debris. White Creek on West Campus will be the focus area.

Participant Arrival Time/Location: 7:45 a.m. in Parking Lot 97 off John Kimbrough Boulevard. You will sign in, pick up equipment and listen to a safety briefing before beginning stream clean activities.

To sign up, go to https://signup.com/go/mcxOMta.

•
Click on the “Sign Up” button (green button)

•
Add your email address, participant name, number of spots (total number of participants), phone number and select your t-shirt size from the dropdown menu.

•
After completing, click “Save” and “Done” (green button).

Signing up a Group?

If you are adding an entire group, please add each person’s name individually, along with their contact information and t-shirt size. Select “Save and Add Another Person” (blue button) for each additional person’s information. This enables everyone to receive updates about the event, as well as any weather-related cancellations.

title: Internship Application Closes
summary_text: The Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Undergraduate Internship Program applications close today. Learn more at sustainability.tamu.edu.
description_text:
The goal of the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Internship Program is to bring undergraduate students from a variety of backgrounds and perspectives together to create a dynamic team that works to create a culture of sustainability at Texas A&M University. Interns work together to increase awareness and education about the three pillars of sustainability: environmental, economic, and social. The team focuses on educating the campus community about topics such as: energy and water use, transportation, food services, construction and built environment, purchasing, recycling, and social sustainability through the development of outreach initiatives and event coordination. Additionally, interns support assessment and planning efforts prioritized by the office.

The Internship Program is open to any TAMU undergraduate student and all majors are encouraged to apply because true sustainability must be an interdisciplinary enterprise.

Applications are open October 6, 2025 – November 9, 2025 at sustainability.tamu.edu.

Interns work together to increase awareness and education about the three pillars of sustainability: environmental, economic, and social. The team focuses on educating the campus community about topics such as: energy and water use, transportation, food services, construction and built environment, purchasing, recycling, and social sustainability through the development of outreach initiatives and event coordination. Additionally, interns support assessment and planning efforts prioritized by the office.

The Internship Program is open to any TAMU undergraduate student and all majors are encouraged to apply because true sustainability must be an interdisciplinary enterprise.

Applications are open March 17th, 2026 – April 14th, 2026 at sustainability.tamu.edu.

summary_text: We’re told that the future is clean energy, but what actually goes into it? In our talk, we dive into the world of energy transition minerals. From policy shifts to community impacts, we’re questioning if a truly clean future exists and what it will take to get there.

title: Caring for What Can’t Speak for Itself: Rights for Animals and Plants for Future Generations
summary_text: This talk examines our role as humans in environmental stewardship, the moral consideration we give to the interests of plants, animals, and future generations, all of which are unable to communicate their needs and interests to us. We argue that plants and animals have intrinsic value, or value within themselves, and that future generations deserve to see the beauty and aesthetics of the planet just as we have. This is based on the belief that all plants and animals have an interest in living, therefore worthy of our consideration in otherwise anthropocentric developments. By rethinking our role in environmental stewardship, we can begin making choices today that protect the world we leave behind.

title: Hullabloom Fest - The Gardens
summary_text: Celebrate the magic of spring — and the pollinators who make it possible — at The Gardens Hullabloom Fest! This joyful community event invites guests of all ages to explore the vibrant world of bees, butterflies, and other garden helpers through hands‑on activities, educational stations, and blooming seasonal displays.
description_text:
Enjoy light refreshments, educational demonstrations, gardening resources, and family‑friendly crafts inspired by wings, petals, and everything in between. And of course we hope you’ll take part in what has become the highlight of the Hullabloom Fest: the butterfly release.

We will have a Sensory Free/Quiet Zone during the Hullabloom Fest for anyone who may want or need a quieter environment at any point during the event.

This event is a free event that is open to the community.

Schedule of Events

9:00 AM – Event Begins

Wander through The Gardens, visit table partners, grab a refreshment, and don’t forget to sign up to release a butterfly.

11:00 AM – Butterfly Release

We will begin handing out butterflies to those who signed up to release one at 10:45 am. Once all butterflies are handed out, we will gather and release on The Event Lawn.

11:30 AM – Event Ends

Thanks for joining us!

Unable to join us? No worries!

Here are a few ways you can still enjoy Spring out in The Gardens!

• Download our scavenger hunt and explore The Gardens as you race to see who can find all of the items first!

• Bring your camera for photos in front of our spring blooms wall at any time this April!

• Create and enjoy one of these delicious spring recipes from Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service’s Dinner Tonight program.

•
Quick Chicken & Spring Vegetables

•
Peach & Blackberry Salad

•
Homemade Basil Pesto

Parking Information

Attendees can park for free in Lots 97 or 100c. More information about our parking options can be found at Parking and Transportation.

title: ASA Sustainability Compass Social
description_text:
Join the Aggie Sustainability Alliance for a fun and interactive lunch experience where we’ll explore the Sustainability Compass through games and conversation. Led by a facilitator, Gitanjali Paul, this session is all about connecting with others, having a few laughs, and discovering new ways to think about sustainability in our everyday lives.

Gitanjali Paul is a teacher by training and an educator by calling. As the founder of Gitanjali Learning Design, she helps mission-driven organizations design learning that moves people from awareness to action on the systems that shape our world. For over 15 years, she has partnered with nonprofits such as Compass Education and the Institute for Humane Education to bring systems thinking and sustainability education to life.

description_text:
Want to see the real-world impact of the Aggie Green Fund? You’re invited to the AGF Project Showcase, where past grant recipients will share how their projects are making Texas A&M a more sustainable place.

This is your opportunity to hear directly from the students, faculty, and staff who are turning innovative ideas into reality. You’ll learn about a range of projects and from every corner of our campus.

Join us to get inspired, ask questions, have a snack, and celebrate the incredible work being done to create a greener campus.

title: Internship Applications Open
summary_text:
The goal of the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Internship Program is to bring undergraduate students from a variety of backgrounds and perspectives together to create a dynamic team that works to create a culture of sustainability at Texas A&M University. Interns work together to increase awareness and education about the three pillars of sustainability: environmental, economic, and social. The team focuses on educating the campus community about topics such as: energy and water use, transportation, food services, construction and built environment, purchasing, recycling, and social sustainability through the development of outreach initiatives and event coordination. Additionally, interns support assessment and planning efforts prioritized by the office.

The Internship Program is open to any TAMU undergraduate student and all majors are encouraged to apply because true sustainability must be an interdisciplinary enterprise.

Applications are open October 5, 2026 – November 2, 2026 at https://sustainability.tamu.edu/team/employment.html

title: Under the Weather: Understanding Texas Disaster Risk and Resilience
summary_text:
Campus Sustainability Month Talk by Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment Student Interns.

This event will take place via zoom, click the link below to register.
description_text: Texas is one of the most disaster affected areas in the United States, in terms of both frequency and cost of disaster occurrences. Explore two of the most devastating Texas disasters: Hill Country Floods and Gulf Coast hurricanes to understand their causes, costs, and recovery. Through these case studies, learn about how rapid climate change increases the risk of disasters and why building community resilience is the best way to move forward.

title: Quality over Quantity: The Impacts of Humanitarian Aid
summary_text:
Campus Sustainability Month Talk by Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment Student Interns.

This event will take place via zoom, click the link below to register.
description_text: This talk examines the importance of integrating logistics and collaboration within the planning stages of humanitarian efforts to generate long-lasting, efficient action. By analyzing the potential risk of certain international development projects and the different factors that influence their success, we challenge listeners to take on a perspective that questions the effectiveness of such investments; one that considers whether a focus on sustainability development and ethical motives can generate a more consolidated-regarding materials and funding- yet efficacious and a qualitative result that benefits all societies, economies, and environments involved.

title: Could A Robot Be Your Next Door Neighbor?
summary_text:
Campus Sustainability Month Talk by Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment Student Interns.

This event will take place via zoom, click the link below to register.
description_text: As the artificial intelligence industry grows, data center developments built by hyperscalers are rapidly expanding into residential backyards, creating environmental and socioeconomic strains for nearby communities. These mega-facilities consume vast resources—generating heavy upfront carbon emissions from concrete and steel construction while exacerbating local air, water, and noise pollution during operation. Furthermore, their power demands strain regional electricity grids, driving up residential utility bills and threatening power reliability. Addressing these localized community impacts requires corporate sustainability disclosures, global and local AI governance, and collaborative policy frameworks.

summary_text:
Campus Sustainability Month Talk by Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment Student Interns.

This event will take place via zoom, click the link below to register.
description_text: Access to healthy and affordable food remains a challenge for many communities across the United States. Learn about the issue of food deserts, why they exist, and how they affect individuals and communities. Discover the connection between food access, nutrition, and overall well-being, as well as potential solutions to create a more accessible and sustainable food system.
